title: Sell Mineral Rights in South Connellsville, PA

metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in South Connellsville, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights in South Connellsville? We're a family buyer, not a landman, and we pay cash for Marcellus interests along the Youghiogheny.
heroLead: South Connellsville sits right across the Youghiogheny from the old coke ovens that built this part of Fayette County, and a surprising number of families here still hold onto mineral rights nobody's touched since the last century.
intro: South Connellsville is a small borough across the river from Connellsville proper, in what used to be the Connellsville coke region. That coal and coke history means a lot of local deeds carry old severed mineral reservations, sometimes coal only, sometimes coal plus oil and gas, going back to when the H.C. Frick Coke Company and others were buying up rights by the thousands of acres in the late 1800s. Untangling exactly what a current-day deed grants you takes real title work, but it's work we do routinely.

Marcellus wet-gas activity has reached into this stretch of Fayette County over the past decade, and tracts near South Connellsville that once seemed like historical curiosities have, in some cases, ended up inside modern drilling units.

sections.heading: Old Coke-Era Deeds Meet Modern Gas Units
paragraphs: If your family's mineral interest here traces back to a coal-era deed, the severance language matters enormously. Some old deeds reserved coal alone and left oil and gas with the surface owner. Others reserved everything below the surface. We read these deeds carefully before ever putting a number in front of you, because getting the severance wrong changes what you actually have to sell.

sections.heading: What a Fair Offer Looks Like
paragraphs: We check whether your tract sits inside an active or permitted unit, review any lease or division order paperwork you have, and account for post-production deductions that may already be reducing your royalty under Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act. From there we make a straightforward cash offer, explained line by line, not a number pulled out of thin air.

faqs.question: How do I know if my old deed reserved oil and gas or just coal?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the specific reservation language in your chain of title. We review the actual recorded deeds at the Fayette County recorder of deeds office to determine exactly what was severed and what remains with your interest.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling right in South Connellsville?
faqs.answer: Activity across Fayette County varies block by block. We check current DEP permits and unit filings against your specific parcel rather than generalizing about the whole borough.

faqs.question: What if I only have a partial, undivided interest?
faqs.answer: That's common on older coke-era tracts split among heirs over multiple generations. We buy fractional and undivided interests and can explain your exact share before you decide anything.
